To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the CFLIB is largely reliable when compared to known spectral standards.

(i) ANN provides plausible spectral classifications for 80\% of the stars in the CFLIB, (ii) missing data in the original database have been successfully restored for 300 stars, (iii) PCA provides a reliable means of selecting the important spectral lines from the original data for the purpose of spectral classification, (iv) a 2-dimensional PCA spectrum supports the notion that neural networks are white noise resistant and perform pattern matching based on meaningful features in the data

(i) 35 stars misclassified by ANN are required to be checked by human experts, (ii) the ANN-PCA spectral classification scheme is 94.44% accurate, and (iii) a scheme has been developed to recover the missing data in the database
In summary, our research is concerned with
major aspects necessary for making optimal use of the CFLIB, such as reliability of spectral types and recovery of missing data.
major issues associated with the reliability of the spectroscopic parameters and special features found in the CFLIB spectra that could influence their classification and other spectral properties.
the reliability of the spectral database at the observational and fundamental theoretical levels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Indo-US stellar library is reliable and can be very useful for detailed study of a wide variety of stellar and Galactic astrophysical problems. 2005 Indian Academy of Sciences.
ANN-based classification of spectra is robust enough to be utilized to produce a reliable spectral classification of stars in the CFLIB.
a significant fraction of stars in the Indo-US stellar spectral library is still awaiting a systematic and detailed examination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

while a large fraction of the stars in the CFLIB have no missing data and can therefore be used directly for stellar population work, another large part of the database is admissible for population work as well, but the user has to be aware of the presence of the missing data. (section 12)
while a number of the stars in the CFLIB need to be verified for spectral types, the broad range of parameters (stellar as well as spectral) is well represented in the database.
while a large fraction of the stars in the CFLIB enjoy good spectral type labels, there is still a considerable fraction that has not yet been well classified.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ANN-variant1, which used data in the wavelength region of 5200-8500 \AA, and ANN-variant2, which used data the region 5200-7500 \AA, can correctly classify 30-50% more spectra than if the full wavelength region is used up to 9464\AA.

, the ANN classification scheme in conjunction with the automated PCA technique has much scope to be used as a reliable automated and objective tool of spectrum classification and can be employed to classify modern and past high-quality spectroscopic surveys.

the CFLIB is now not only a reliable tool to classify a large number of stars in a multi-class setup easily and efficiently, but can also be used as a data-mining tool to extract low dimensional features from the data to reconstruct the missing or obscured data.
